newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX to begin electric, other strip trade Sept 12.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX to begin electric, other strip trade Sept 12.

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) said traders will be able to trade gasoline, heating oil and both electricity futures contracts in calendar strips beginning September 12, while copper futures strip trade will begin September 20.
Under the strip trade offer, participants will be able to buy or sell the same number of futures contracts for consecutive months in a single transaction, NYMEX said in a statement.
Electricity, heating oil and gasoline strips will be traded the same way as NYMEX natural gas and crude oil strips are, NYMEX said.
Trade will involve a single, agreed upon differential to the previous day's settlement price for each of the contracts.
Copper strips will be traded at an average price for the entire strip.
Once a strip trade has been executed, positions in each month will be treated as any other futures contracts for those months, NYMEX said.
The number of months involved in the strip can range from two to 24 for copper, from two to 18 for electricity and from two to 12 for gasoline.

"This method of trading has proven successful in assisting our commercial participants in their long-term planning by enabling them to protect their extended market exposure at an average price over that period of time," NYMEX president Patrick Thompson said in the statement.
